extracted.intended_audience: exchange finance and compliance staff, SEC/market regulators, market participants reviewing fee justification
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for allocating exchange costs to 1Gb/10Gb ULL connectivity and to FIX/MEO ports, including methodology, cost drivers, percentages, and per-connection cost calculations used to justify connectivity and port fees in a regulatory filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee time allocation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Twice a year, and as needed with additional new hires and new project initiatives, managers and department heads assign a percentage of time to every employee and then allocate that time amongst the Exchange and its affiliated markets to determine each market's individual Human Resources expense. Managers and department heads then assign a percentage of each employee's time allocated to the Exchange into buckets including network connectivity, ports, market data, and other exchange services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every employee is 100% allocated so there is no double counting between the Exchange and its affiliated markets; consult with employees as needed when assigning percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Resources allocation to connectivity — primary personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate HR costs for employees whose functions include providing and maintaining physical connectivity and performance thereof (primarily the Exchange's network infrastructure team) to connectivity cost drivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent company allocates costs to the Exchange and affiliates; a portion allocated to the Exchange is then allocated to connectivity. Use weighted average percentages (example: 58% for 10Gb ULL and 2.0% for 1Gb connectivity for the primary group). Include functions such as installation, configuration, maintenance, hardware access, software upgrades, vulnerability remediation, performance and capacity management, R&D, and internal reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Resources allocation to connectivity — ancillary personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate HR costs for a limited subset of personnel with ancillary functions related to establishing and maintaining connectivity (such as information security, sales, membership, and finance) on an employee-by-employee basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include personnel who support functions related to providing physical connectivity; apply a smaller allocation of such employees' time to 10Gb ULL connectivity (e.g., less than 37%). Require a direct nexus (e.g., sales person selling connections, finance billing, information security ensuring security).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document allocations via consultation and reasonableness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of Human Resources cost are determined by consulting department leaders to identify employees involved in connectivity tasks and confirming proposed allocations are reasonable based on the percentage of time devoted to those tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold meetings with senior management, department heads, and finance to determine allocation amounts; keep records of consultations and rationales as support for allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior executive time allocation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior level executives' time is allocated to connectivity-related Human Resources costs only to the extent they are involved in overseeing tasks related to providing physical connectivity or managing personnel responsible for such tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not broadly allocate executive time unless direct oversight or management of connectivity responsibilities exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blended compensation rate for HR costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Resources cost is calculated using a blended rate of compensation reflecting salary, equity and bonus compensation, benefits, payroll taxes, and 401(k) matching contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a comprehensive blended rate (not simply base salary) when converting allocated time percentages into dollar HR costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain deviations via business/technical initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: When an allocation percentage differs materially from affiliates, explain the difference based on current and anticipated business and technology initiatives, technical architecture, market structure, or other marketplace-specific factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples (e.g., enhancements to routing options, adding direct market data connectivity, additional risk controls) to justify higher allocations versus affiliates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivity cost driver definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Connectivity cost driver includes external fees paid to connect to other exchanges and third parties, cabling, and switches required to operate the Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus narrowly on technology used to complete connections to the Exchange and to connect to external markets; note that connectivity is required to receive market data and to run the matching engine in compliance with Regulation NMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and justification of third‑party connectivity providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and include costs for third-party connectivity providers that connect the Exchange to other national securities exchanges, NASDAQ UTP, and CTA/CQ Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that without these providers the Exchange could not operate; note that such providers often serve most U.S. exchanges and that expenses are (in part) recouped by charging for 1Gb and 10Gb ULL connectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet services and external market data allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include internet services (third-party providers of internet, fiber, and bandwidth between data centers and offices) and external market data fees as cost drivers for connectivity because market data is necessary for services related to connectivity (e.g., risk checks performed prior to execution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate an amount of these costs to 1Gb and 10Gb connectivity when market data is consumed at the matching engine or port level for validations (e.g., NBBO checks, trading collars, halts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Center allocation to connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate data center costs (dedicated space, security, cooling, power) to physical connectivity because leased third-party data center space and equipment are direct costs of providing physical access to the Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High percentage allocations are appropriate (example: 62% to 1Gb/10Gb connectivity) because without dedicated presence in data centers physical connectivity has no value to market participants; explain differences in dollar amounts vs percentages if a market's total allocation differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardware and Software maintenance and license allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate costs for hardware and software licenses used to operate and monitor physical assets necessary to offer physical connectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for platform-specific or market-specific licenses that cannot be shared across affiliates (e.g., equities-specific licenses) and justify higher allocations when licenses are unique to a market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation valuation and period
rubrics_metrics.description: Value physical assets, software, and hardware at cost and depreciate or lease them over periods ranging from three to five years; include assets used for testing and monitoring and budgeted capitalized improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute depreciation narrowly to connectivity-related assets (example allocations: 73.6% to 10Gb ULL; 2.5% to 1Gb) and explain deviations from affiliates due to asset age or new system enhancements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocated shared expenses multi-layered process
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate general shared expenses by first allocating among the Exchange and affiliated markets, then across the Exchange's core services (including connectivity), and finally to sub-categories (e.g., 10Gb ULL connectivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine subcategory percentages by looking at percentage allocations of each cost driver, hold meetings with senior management/department heads/finance, and ensure allocations are not double-counted; provide rationale tying allocations to operational importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 50% allocation rule for general shared expenses to 10Gb ULL
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate 50% of the portion of general shared expenses assigned to physical connectivity to 10Gb ULL connectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify the 50% as reasonable because it aligns with other cost driver allocations and reflects strategic importance of 10Gb ULL as a premium-product network delivering high performance and value-add monitoring/reporting services; note this may be higher than allocations for other port types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid full allocation to single core service / prevent double-counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allocate any expenses in full to any core services and ensure there is no double-counting of expenses across services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate applicable cost drivers across core services and use consistent methodology when the same cost supports multiple products (e.g., connectivity and proprietary data feeds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-connection cost calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute approximate cost per connection by dividing total monthly allocated cost for a connectivity type by the number of physical connections maintained at the time pricing was determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: total monthly 10Gb cost $1,477,233 ÷ 90 connections = ~$16,414/month per 10Gb connection; round per-connection results to nearest dollar. Use actual number of connections as a quantifiable allocation basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ports (FIX and MEO) HR allocation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: For FIX and MEO Ports, calculate HR costs by allocating employee time for those providing and maintaining ports (technical operations, market operations, software engineering) and a limited subset of ancillary personnel on an employee-by-employee basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult department leaders to confirm reasonable percentage of time devoted to ports; allocate senior executive time only if overseeing port-related personnel; use blended compensation rate as with connectivity. Example allocations: ~5.2% of overall HR to FIX Ports, ~17.2% to MEO Ports.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEO vs FIX cost-differentiation rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that MEO Ports typically incur higher costs than FIX Ports because MEO is a customizable, in‑house binary interface requiring more development, maintenance, dedicated hardware, and support and is aimed at latency-sensitive market makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect higher allocations for HR, depreciation, and allocated shared expenses for MEO Ports; cite technical reasons (dedicated core server per MEO port vs. 3–5 FIX connections per server, higher bandwidth consumption) when justifying higher MEO fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation allocation for ports
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate depreciation for hardware and in-house developed software used to provide FIX and MEO Ports; value assets at cost and depreciate over 3–5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example allocations: 2.00% of depreciation to FIX Ports and 6.60% to MEO Ports; explain differences due to in-house development and more dedicated hardware for MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocated shared expense components for ports
rubrics_metrics.description: Include general shared expenses (office occupancy and overhead, utilities, recruiting and training, marketing, professional fees, telecommunications, and a portion of directors' compensation) as allocable costs to FIX and MEO Ports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate based on weighted costs attributable to each core service; example allocations might show lower shared-expense percentage for ports (e.g., 5.2%) than for physical connectivity, and smaller director-compensation portion (<20% allocated to ports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding and reporting transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting allocated annual and monthly costs, document rounding methods and footnote rounding explanations when dividing annual costs to monthly or per‑unit figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide footnotes explaining rounding of annual and monthly costs and rounding to nearest dollar when computing per-port or per-connection prices.
